metric.build_test_integration.deduction_rationale: 6-point deduction applied for documented fragmentation/friction: coexistence of XCTest and the newer Swift Testing library during a multi-year transition, platform-specific (Linux vs Apple) historical divergence (LinuxMain generation), and non-trivial extra tooling required for full iOS-target build+test workflows outside of pure command-line SwiftPM.

citation.quote: The Swift Package Manager integrates directly with XCTest to provide a streamlined experience for unit testing SwiftPM packages.

observations.finding: Swift Package Manager is the official build tool and provides a single command that both builds and runs the full test suite.

citation.quote: The testing library has experimental integration with Swift Package Manager's

observations.finding: XCTest is the long-standing native framework, and Apple's newer 'Swift Testing' library has experimental integration directly into the swift test command, alongside XCTest, though the two-framework transition period and platform caveats (e.g. Linux LinuxMain generation historically, experimental flags) introduce some fragmentation.

citation.quote: It feels like it lives in a grey area in between public interface and and implementation detail.

observations.finding: swift test supports a built-in --enable-code-coverage flag producing coverage JSON, and third-party actions (e.g. spm-lcov-action, swift-codecov-action) convert this into standard formats for CI, though the mechanism is documented as somewhat under-specified for end-to-end use ('a grey area... --help leaves you in the dark').

citation.quote: there is built-in support for parallel execution (you can even specify the number of workers), you can also filter what to run by test target

observations.finding: SwiftPM has built-in support for parallel test execution with configurable worker counts, listing available tests, and filtering by regular expression.

citation.quote: Every commit to main is validated automatically using GitHub Actions.

observations.finding: GitHub Actions integration for Swift packages (setup-swift, official swift Docker images, xcodebuild-based iOS/macOS CI recipes) is well documented and widely used, e.g. tests validated automatically per commit via GitHub Actions, but platform-specific caveats exist: full iOS package testing historically required Xcode-project generation rather than pure SwiftPM, and coverage tooling for non-Apple products (Codecov) needs extra bundling/config work.

rubric.description: Frozen rubric applied identically to all 10 languages in this metric family. Score 0-100 composed of five equally-weighted 0-20 sub-scores: (1) presence of an official/standard build tool with a unified build+test entrypoint, (2) a native unit-test framework integrated into that tool, (3) built-in code coverage support, (4) parallel/filterable test execution, (5) first-class, low-friction CI ecosystem support (official GitHub Actions, coverage-upload integrations, cross-platform CI recipes).
rubric.scale: 0=capability absent or requires bespoke non-standard tooling; 10=capability exists but with significant friction/fragmentation; 20=capability is standard, official, low-friction

metric.documentation_quality.deduction_rationale: 9-point deduction applied because official third-party-package documentation coverage is inconsistent across the ecosystem (Swift Package Index notes 'no gatekeeping or quality threshold' for included packages and DocC hosting requires opt-in configuration per package, so uniform first-party-quality docs are not guaranteed ecosystem-wide even though the core language/toolchain documentation is strong).

citation.quote: We encourage you to participate in translating The Swift Programming Language into other languages.

observations.finding: Swift.org hosts an official 'Language reference' (The Swift Programming Language), maintained by the project with an open community translation process.

citation.quote: Much of Apple's developer documentation, from Reference documentation to Tutorials, and long-form content is built using Swift-DocC.

observations.finding: Apple's developer documentation and much of the reference documentation for Swift frameworks/packages is built and published using the official Swift-DocC toolchain.

citation.quote: Swift-DocC provides an effortless way to author great documentation alongside your code, and generate comprehensive documentation websites for Swift codebases.

observations.finding: Swift-DocC is an actively developed, open-sourced official documentation compiler supporting API doc comments, long-form articles, and tutorials, and is integrated into Xcode and the wider package ecosystem (e.g. Swift Package Index can build and host DocC docs for indexed packages).

citation.quote: This repository hosts multiple DocC catalogs that provide the source location for documentation content for the Swift project, hosted at www.swift.org.

observations.finding: Swift-DocC explicitly supports step-by-step tutorials with integrated images as part of official documentation authoring, and the Swift.org docs repository (swiftlang/docs) collects documentation content hosted at swift.org.
The swiftlang/docs repository shows recent activity (updated within the last two weeks of the snapshot date) and Swift-DocC is described by its maintainers as being actively developed.

rubric.description: Frozen rubric applied identically to all 10 languages in this metric family. Score 0-100 composed of five equally-weighted 0-20 sub-scores: (1) an official language reference maintained by the language steward, (2) official standard-library/API reference documentation, (3) a maintained, integrated documentation-generation toolchain for the ecosystem, (4) official tutorials/learning materials, (5) evidence of active maintenance/currency of the documentation.
rubric.scale: 0=no official documentation; 10=exists but stale/incomplete/third-party only; 20=official, current, comprehensive

supporting_citation.quote: There's no gatekeeping or quality threshold to be included in the Swift Package Index.
